A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Content can be matched across the added sections and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original contract-optimization results and sensitivity analyses using AlpacaEval and SWE-Bench data in Section 6 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains those original analyses and adds provider-utility and contract-cost results in Appendix H.3.2 and Figure 10.

M1.justification: The two-tier inspection/payment framework, optimization algorithms, and CoMI, UMI, CoNI, and UNI variants are unchanged. The additional analyses do not modify the proposed procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use AlpacaEval 2.0 with 805 prompts and SWE-Bench bash-only with 500 issues. The added analyses remain within the existing coding scenario; varying test-suite size does not introduce new task coverage.

E2.justification: The four AlpacaEval baselines remain unchanged. v2 Figure 8 expands the reported SWE-Bench policy comparison beyond Figure 5's three displayed policies, including p=(0,1,1) and p=(1,1,1).

E3.justification: v2 adds an evaluation varying inspected outcome-space size while targeting GPT-5 and measuring agent utility, internal cost, inspection cost, and total principal cost (Appendix H.3.2). The existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Figure 10 analysis examines how evaluation informativeness affects provider information rent and the components of contract cost. The existing reward, inspection-cost, bootstrap, Beta-Binomial, and Dirichlet sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 100 bootstrap repetitions, standard-deviation bars, binomial and bootstrap-quantile intervals, and 95% t-based confidence bands. No new run-count, seed, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports zero-inspection-cost ties among three policies and Figure 10's generally declining provider utility with an upward jump at a policy transition. Existing headline results remain unchanged, including $1.00 principal utility and a 14% advantage over the closest non-adaptive baseline on AlpacaEval.

T1.justification: The mathematical framework, theorem statements, and tractability, hardness, and randomized-inspection proofs are unchanged after matching appendix renumbering. The new provider-utility discussion supplies interpretation rather than a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contribution statements retain the same claims about tractability, hardness, randomized contracts, and empirical benefits. The appendix additions do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B substantially expands applicability qualifications to cover evaluation gaming, finite action spaces, user bargaining power, and known stationary score distributions. New Appendix C explains when adaptivity can help or hurt providers through changes in information rent, extending the previous principal-centered interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 corrects the swapped AlpacaEval length-condition labels to agree with Figure 4, adds an explicit SWE-Bench data-directory link, and states that archived API pricing is included in supplementary materials. Code, software, hardware, and runtime disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The expanded limitations cite additional work on robust and online contract design, including Carroll, Ho and colleagues, and Zhu and colleagues, plus forecasting evaluation and enterprise-market sources. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands Appendix B, inserts an Agent's Utility appendix, and renames and renumbers subsequent appendices. It also makes limited wording corrections and updates publication and acknowledgment text; the main narrative is largely preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 8 and 10 for the expanded policy comparison and provider-utility/cost analysis. The former Figure 8 becomes Figure 9 with minor display edits, and Figure 6 relocates within the appendix. Existing main figures and the model-data table are retained.

improvement.justification: The expanded limitations and provider-utility analysis clarify applicability and economic consequences, while corrected AlpacaEval labels improve consistency. These provide a limited net improvement. One new weakness remains: Appendix C describes provider utility as monotonically decreasing, although Figure 10 shows an upward policy-transition jump acknowledged in Appendix H.3.2.
